subject.title: [Feature]: Add per-channel identity override for Discord bindings

question: Should OpenClaw support this as binding-level nickname mutation, Discord webhook persona delivery, a broader agent identity surface, or keep it out of core for now?
rationale: The request affects public config shape, Discord identity/security boundaries, and existing adjacent identity proposals, so automation should not choose the product model or credential boundary.

options.title: Webhook Persona Delivery
options.body: Add an explicit Discord plugin-owned webhook/persona delivery path for routed replies, with credential handling and loop/fallback semantics defined up front.

options.title: Self-Profile Only
options.body: Route this request into the separate bot self-profile work and decline per-message or per-binding visible identity for ordinary replies.

options.title: Close As Out Of Scope
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's Discord replies on configured bot accounts and require separate Discord bots or external webhooks for distinct visible identities.

recommendation.title: Webhook Persona Delivery
recommendation.body: Add an explicit Discord plugin-owned webhook/persona delivery path for routed replies, with credential handling and loop/fallback semantics defined up front.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent thread-bound Discord webhook/persona work is the closest existing implementation pattern for routed visible identity.
